title: Troubleshooting Siphonage: The Hidden Cause of Smelly Drains
description: When P-traps lose their water seal, sewer gas creeps into living spaces. A common culprit is poor drain ventilation, not just a leaking trap. As water flows through an unvented or clogged vent pipe, it creates a negative pressure vacuum that pulls the water seal out of nearby traps. To troubleshoot, inspect vent stacks on the roof for bird nests, leaf buildup, or ice dams. Verifying atmospheric pressure balance protects trap seals and prevents sewer gas backflow. Always check local plumbing codes for proper vent sizing and distance limits relative to the fixture trap.

Troubleshooting Siphonage: The Hidden Cause of Smelly Drains

When P-traps lose their water seal, sewer gas creeps into living spaces. A common culprit is poor drain ventilation, not just a leaking trap. As water flows through an unvented or clogged vent pipe, it creates a negative pressure vacuum that pulls the water seal out of nearby traps. To troubleshoot, inspect vent stacks on the roof for bird nests, leaf buildup, or ice dams. Verifying atmospheric pressure balance protects trap seals and prevents sewer gas backflow. Always check local plumbing codes for proper vent sizing and distance limits relative to the fixture trap.
